$comment: Maps the Content Contract audience vocabulary (ai/openwebui/knowledge/company-wiki/tools/wiki-schema.json)
onto the Open WebUI groups that actually exist on the live instance.
This is the artifact llm-knowledge-base-plan.md Phase 0 calls 'Define the audience and
sensitivity vocabulary and its exact Open WebUI group mapping'. upload_kb.py REFUSES to
publish a collection needing a mapping this file does not carry: the plan's rule is that a
document cannot be published when its metadata has no valid group mapping, so failing closed
is the compliant behavior.
The vocabulary is tier-shaped (erisa-member / erisa-team-lead / erisa-manager) while the live
groups are function-shaped (Erisa - Creator / Erisa - Campaign). That mismatch is why this
file is an explicit reviewed decision rather than something a script infers.
Group NAMES are resolved to ids at run time against GET /api/v1/groups/, so a rename fails
loudly instead of silently granting nothing.
approved_scope: ERISA only. Every other pillar is deliberately unmapped and fails closed.

$comment: Applied to every collection on top of the audience-derived grants.
'sensitivity_scoped_read' grants read only when EVERY file in the collection sits
within the listed sensitivity tiers. It is intentionally EMPTY: org-general was the
only candidate, and its automatic grant is suspended pending an ownership decision.
The mechanism is kept because it is how that decision gets implemented once made.
Collections allowed to publish WITHOUT derived grants, via --manual-grants-exception.
Membership here is the authorization; the caller's free-text reason is not. Adding a
collection is a reviewed change -- cite the document that approves it.

erisa-tiers-to-creator-only: All three ERISA tiers map to 'Erisa - Creator' alone, NOT to 'Erisa - Campaign'.
This reproduces the grants erisa-platform-ops-sop already had, so approving this file
changed nobody's access. Revisit if the Campaign team needs Platform PoC content: the
SOP does cover campaign incentive work, so widening is defensible — but it is a widening
and belongs here as an explicit edit, not as an inference at run time.
unmapped-by-design: No owner has decided how these map onto the live functional groups
(Commerce - Operation / Commerce - Sales, Erify - Onset / Erify - Offset), and the live
'Management team' group has no vocabulary entry at all. Any collection whose audiences
touch these will be refused publication until an owner adds them here. That is the
org-general-automatic-grant-suspended: org-general (the GM, read-only) receives NO automatic grant, on any collection.
wiki-schema.json used to say it was auto-granted 'regardless of sensitivity'. That
contradicted the sensitivity ladder in the same file: 'department' means 'one pillar
only' and 'restricted' means 'named leadership groups only', neither of which can
include the GM. Only 'internal' is defined as reaching org-general.
Rather than substitute a scope the owner has not chosen, the automatic grant is
withdrawn entirely and the question left open. That keeps every surface stating the
same thing -- no automatic grant -- instead of two documents implying different access.
Nothing is lost: the rule was never implemented. validate-wiki only ever expanded a
document's own audiences, so no collection has ever received org-general this way.
Where the GM should have access, grant it explicitly on that collection.
